messages:
mike: Heads up — noticed drift between partner hourly snapshots and our eventstream aggregation for the last 3 days. example: partner shows -8 credits at 12:00 UTC but our ledger has +2. anyone seen this pattern?

anya: ugh yep saw a spike yesterday. looks like some events are being attributed to the previous hour. maybe timezone or late-arrival bucketing? :thinking_face:

samir: quick note: partner sends usage_timestamp in local tz (PST) and an arrival_ts. our pipeline currently buckets using arrival_ts for "hourly snapshot" ingest. that could shift events across hour boundaries during late batches.

jess: can you paste an example payload? we should confirm which field they expect us to use for the hour key.

mike: sample payload from partner:```
{
  "usage_timestamp": "2026-03-21T11:58:32-07:00",
  "usage_units": 120,
  "meter_id": "partner.embed.v1",
  "ingest_arrival_ts": "2026-03-21T19:02:05Z"
}
```

liam: so they intend usage_timestamp -> local hour bucket (11:00-12:00 PST). our hourly snapshot job truncates ingest_arrival_ts to UTC hour -> 19:00 UTC which maps to 12:00 PST. off by one hour when events arrive late across DST boundary?

samir: exactly. two problems: 1) we use arrival_ts for snapshotting by default, 2) some partners expect us to normalize to their published usage_timestamp timezone before bucketing. both need a contract.

anya: proposal: for partner-metered contracts, add a field in the webhook schema: "preferred_bucket_strategy": ["usage_timestamp","arrival_timestamp","partner_hour_local"]. default stays arrival_timestamp to preserve existing behavior. we can opt partners into usage_timestamp bucket semantics.

jess: that seems reasonable. for immediate recon, can we run a backfill that reassigns events where abs(arrival - usage) > 5 minutes? query to surface candidates:```sql
SELECT id, usage_timestamp, ingest_arrival_ts, usage_units
FROM partner_events
WHERE DATE_TRUNC('hour', usage_timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') != DATE_TRUNC('hour', ingest_arrival_ts)
  AND ingest_arrival_ts > usage_timestamp + INTERVAL '5 minutes'
LIMIT 1000;
```

mike: run that and share results in this thread. also flag any negative deltas in the hourly snapshot table.

marketplace-bot: nightly snapshot job completed: hourly_snapshot(2026-03-21T12:00:00Z) -> 0 mismatches found (baseline). manual check recommended for partner=si-integrator-9.

liam: note — partner has DST switch in their region next week. we should avoid relying on local tz offsets. better to standardize on usage_timestamp normalized to UTC in the contract.

samir: agreed. operational plan: 1) run the SQL above, 2) build a small backfill that re-buckets identified events using usage_timestamp->UTC hour, 3) update partner contract & webhook schema with preferred_bucket_strategy option, and 4) add automated alerts when >0.5% of events in an hour are re-bucketed.

anya: i can take 1 and 2 today. jess can you own schema update + docs? mike can you ping SIs and get sign-off?

jess: on it. will draft a short compatibility note and include example migration (we need to surface best-effort mapping for partners who don't provide timezone info).

mike: thx. @liam can you add a quick unit test to the snapshot job to assert we're using the configured bucket strategy? small change, prevents regression.

liam: yep will add test and an integration test that simulates late arrivals.

mike: timeline?

anya: I should have the backfill results and a PR for the backfill by EOD.

jess: i'll have schema PR by tomorrow morning and a partner-facing note draft.

samir: i'll stand by to review the backfill for perf impact. if anything > 10k rows/hour we should do staged windows.

mike: perfect. tagging this as actioned — if anyone finds new mismatches, drop CSVs here. thanks :thumbsup:
